transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Hi, thanks. Um… I guess I’m here because I’ve been having trouble keeping my attention on work, more than I’d like to admit. I’m a secondary school teacher, and I’ll sit down with a stack of essays or a curriculum document, genuinely intending to get through it, and then maybe ten minutes later I realize I’ve just been staring at the same page. My mind’s off on three different things and I’m not really taking in what’s in front of me. It’s probably not the worst thing, but it’s been happening enough that I thought I should ask about it.
Have you noticed feeling down, hopeless, or losing interest in things you usually enjoy around the same time these attention problems started?

Um… I don’t think so, not really. I mean, I get frustrated with myself when I’m not getting things done, but I wouldn’t say I’ve been feeling hopeless or that I’ve stopped enjoying things. At least, nothing like that that I’ve clearly noticed. Does that make sense?
Have you noticed yourself feeling restless, fidgety, or having trouble staying seated, especially during tasks that require focus?

Um… not especially, I don’t think. I’m not usually the sort of person who’s up and pacing around or unable to sit still. I might shift in my chair or tap a pen now and then, but I wouldn’t say it’s a big thing or something people comment on. Is that the kind of thing you mean?
Have you found yourself interrupting others often, talking more than usual, or acting on impulse without thinking things through?

Um… no, I don’t think that’s really me. I’m usually pretty conscious about not cutting people off, especially at work. I might occasionally jump in if I’m worried I’ll forget what I was going to say, but not in a way that feels out of control or that people have pointed out. And I wouldn’t say I’m acting on impulse much, at least not that I’ve noticed.
Do you ever feel unusually restless or hyperactive in other situations, like when you’re at home, trying to relax, or in social settings?

Not really, no. At home I’m usually able to sit and relax, or at least I don’t feel like I’m buzzing or need to be moving all the time. Socially, I don’t think I come across as hyper or anything. I might get a bit mentally distracted, but physically restless… no, I wouldn’t say that’s a major thing for me. Is that answering what you’re asking?
Do you also find it hard to focus or get distracted easily in other situations, like when you're at home doing something quiet or trying to follow a conversation with friends?

Yeah… I think that’s probably more where I struggle, honestly. Not so much being physically restless, but staying with something mentally.

Like, the main reason I came in is I can sit down with a stack of essays or a curriculum document fully intending to get through it, and then ten minutes later I realize I’ve just been staring at the same page. My mind’s gone off in three different directions and I haven’t really taken in what I’m reading. It feels a bit embarrassing to say, because I’m trying to do the work, it’s not that I don’t care.

At home or in conversations, it can happen too, though I try to cover it. I’ll realize I’ve missed part of what someone said and then I’m sort of trying to piece it together without making it obvious. Does that make sense?
Have you ever had difficulty waiting your turn or felt the need to act quickly without thinking, especially in situations where you needed to be patient or deliberate?

I don’t think that’s a big issue for me, no. I mean, I can get a bit impatient internally, like anyone, but I’m usually pretty careful about waiting my turn and not pushing ahead.

With decisions, I tend to overthink more than act too quickly, if anything. I wouldn’t want to say “never,” but I can’t think of many situations where I’ve done something impulsive and then thought, oh, I really should’ve slowed down. Is that the sort of thing you mean?
Do you often feel anxious, worried, or overwhelmed, especially when you’re trying to focus on tasks?

I’m not sure, honestly. I mean, I do get overwhelmed sometimes when I’m trying to get something done, but I don’t know if I’d call it anxiety exactly.

It’s more like… I notice I’m not focusing, and then I start worrying that I’m wasting time or not doing it properly, which probably makes it harder. But I wouldn’t want to overstate it. I’m not panicking or anything. It’s just a bit of pressure building up, if that makes sense.

Can you think of a time when you were doing something that really interested you or that you enjoyed—like a hobby, a show you like, or reading something fun—where you still found your mind wandering or had trouble staying focused?

Yeah… I think so. I mean, it’s maybe not as bad if it’s something I enjoy, but it still happens.

The clearest example is probably with reading or watching something I actually want to follow. I’ll sit down thinking, right, I’m interested in this, this should be easy, and then after a few minutes I realize I’ve been looking at the page or the screen but not really taking it in. My thoughts have gone off somewhere else, and I have to go back over it.

It’s similar to what I was saying about work, really — I can sit down with essays or a curriculum document fully intending to get through it, and then ten minutes later I’m still on the same bit, thinking about three other things. I feel a bit silly saying that because I don’t want it to sound like I’m just not trying, but it does happen even when I’m making an effort.
Have you noticed feeling unusually tired or low on energy, even when you haven’t been doing anything physically demanding?

Not particularly, I don’t think. I mean, I get tired at the end of a school day, but that feels fairly normal given the job.

I wouldn’t say I’m unusually low on energy when I haven’t done much physically. If anything, it’s more that I can feel mentally worn out sometimes, but I’m not sure that’s what you mean. Does that answer it properly?
Do you ever feel an internal sense of restlessness, like your mind is constantly going even when you want to focus or relax?

I don’t know, really. I wouldn’t say I feel physically restless, if that’s what you mean.

My mind can feel busy sometimes, like I’m thinking about what I need to do or what I haven’t done, but I’m not sure if that’s unusual or just normal. When I try to relax, I can usually sit still, though I might have thoughts going on in the background.

Is that the sort of thing you mean?
Do you ever feel like your thoughts are racing or jumping around, making it hard for you to focus or relax, even if you’re not physically restless?

Yeah… I think that’s probably a fair way of putting it, though I don’t know if I’d call it “racing” exactly.

It’s more like I sit down to focus — say with a stack of essays or a curriculum document — and I genuinely mean to get on with it. Then after maybe ten minutes I notice I’ve just been staring at the same page, and my mind’s gone off in three different directions. I’m thinking about other things rather than actually taking in what’s in front of me.

It’s a bit frustrating, because I’m not trying to avoid it. I just sort of… lose the thread. Does that make sense?
Can you recall if you're able to stay fully engaged in activities that really interest you, like a favorite show or a hobby, or do you still find your attention drifting even then?

I suppose with things I’m really interested in, it’s better… or at least it feels less noticeable.

But the main thing that brought me in is more with work tasks, really. I can sit down with a stack of essays or a curriculum document fully intending to get through it, and then after maybe ten minutes I realise I’ve been staring at the same page. My mind’s gone off onto three other things, and I’m barely taking in what’s in front of me.

I don’t mean that I’m not trying, because I am. It just sort of slips away from me. I’m not sure if that answers the question about hobbies exactly.
Looking back, were you someone who had trouble focusing or staying on task when you were a child, say before you were 12 years old?

I think… yes, probably. I don’t want to overstate it, because I did alright academically, but even in primary school my reports had comments like “bright but careless” or that I didn’t finish work unless someone was keeping a close eye on me.

And my parents used to find worksheets crumpled up in my backpack that I’d apparently forgotten to hand in. I suppose at the time it was treated as me being a bit disorganised or not trying hard enough, maybe. Does that count as the sort of thing you’re asking about?
